genxml.title: Hub register arrays whose extent is a fact of its own
genxml.doc: Runs of consecutive Hub registers seen as one array each, so that the end of the run is data. Each entry overlaps the registers listed one by one in the other Hub units, which carry the individual names; the two views describe the same storage. The offsets, names and counts come from the IRIX register headers and register table named in each entry.

struct.name: PI_GFX_WINDOW
struct.doc: The graphics registers of both processor slots as one window: page, credit counter, bias, interrupt counter and interrupt comparator for slot A, then the same five for slot B. The source gives the distance between the two sets as the offset of the slot B page from the slot A page. The entries are also listed one by one under their own names; this is the same storage seen as an array, so that its extent is data.

struct.name: MD_PERF_CNT
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub memory/directory header: MD_PERF_CNT0 to MD_PERF_CNT5
struct.doc: The six memory/directory performance counters as one array. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption.

struct.name: MD_UREG0
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub memory/directory header: MD_UREG0_0 to MD_UREG0_7
struct.doc: The eight microcontroller and UART 0 registers as one array. The same storage is listed one by one where the census reaches it. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption.

struct.name: MD_UREG1
struct.doc: The sixteen microcontroller and UART 1 registers as one array. They are also listed one by one under their own names; this is the same storage seen as an array, so that its extent is data. On the Origin 200 (the SN00 variant) the kernel's per-processor LED macro writes the LED of slice 0 at element 0 and the LED of slice 1 at element 4, a spacing of four elements per slice; other Hub variants use the separate LED registers. The IRIX register table gives read and write access for the entries it lists (0, 1 and 15) and the header gives all sixteen the same description.

struct.name: IIO_IOPRB
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub I/O header: IIO_IOPRB_0 to IIO_IOPRB_F, IIO_NUM_IPRBS; the iprb_t structure
struct.doc: The nine I/O partial-request buffer entries (0, then 8 to f) as one array; entry 0 sits at the first offset and entries 8 to f follow, eight bytes apart. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption. The header says the nak and overflow counters are status fields to be used only when cleaning up after errors.

struct.name: IIO_PRTE
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub I/O header: IIO_PRTE_0, IIO_PRTE(x), IIO_NUM_PRTES; the iprte_a structure
struct.doc: The eight PIO read address table entries as one array. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption.

struct.name: NI_AGE
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub network interface header: NI_AGE_CPU0_MEMORY to NI_AGE_IO_PIO (NI_AGE_REG_MIN, NI_AGE_REG_MAX)
struct.doc: The eight network age-control registers as one array: CPU 0 memory, CPU 0 PIO, CPU 1 memory, CPU 1 PIO, GBR memory, GBR PIO, I/O memory, I/O PIO, in that order. The same storage is listed one by one in the network interface unit, where the field layout sits. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption.

struct.name: NI_META_TABLE
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub network interface header: NI_META_TABLE(x), NI_META_ENTRIES, NMT_EXIT_PORT_MASK
struct.doc: The 32-entry meta routing table as one array, replacing the split of the first entry and the other 31. Each entry holds the exit port. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption.

struct.name: NI_LOCAL_TABLE
struct.from: Linux SN0 Hub network interface header: NI_LOCAL_TABLE(x), NI_LOCAL_ENTRIES, NLT_EXIT_PORT_MASK
struct.doc: The 16-entry local routing table as one array, replacing the split of the first entry and the other 15. Each entry holds the exit port. The header gives no access type, so rw is an assumption.
